problem: The two scale factors are attached to the wrong axes. With θ as the vertical field of view and a = width/height, the vertical scale is the larger one, 1/tan(θ/2), and the horizontal scale is 1/(a·tan(θ/2)). The chapter gives x the 1/tan(θ/2) factor and y the 1/(a·tan(θ/2)) factor, which is backwards: a student who transposes this matrix gets a wrongly stretched image on any non-square viewport.
fix: Write: P scales y by 1/tan(θ/2) and x by 1/(a·tan(θ/2)), where θ is the vertical field of view and a = width/height.

where: Section 2 (look-at) versus Section 3 (camera at origin looking along +z)
problem: The chapter switches camera convention without saying so. Section 2 ends with 'a point straight ahead of the camera now has x = y = 0 and negative z', i.e. the standard camera looks along −z. Section 3 opens with 'Put the camera at the origin looking along +z' and writes x′ = f·x/z, which only works with positive z in front. The exam trap itself warns against mixing conventions, so the chapter contradicts its own advice and a student cannot tell which sign to use in the exam.
fix: Pick one convention and state it once. Either keep the −z-forward camera and write x′ = f·x/(−z), y′ = f·y/(−z) in Section 3, or add one sentence at the start of Section 3: 'This section uses a +z-forward camera, so points in front have positive z; the image-plane formulas below use that convention.'

problem: 'After the divide, every visible point lies in NDC ... Hardware clips triangles against these planes' places clipping after the perspective divide, which contradicts Section 1 ('Clipping needs depth in front of the camera, so it comes before the divide'). Hardware clips in clip space against the near plane before dividing.
fix: Say: hardware clips against the near plane in clip space, before the divide, testing w > 0; the NDC bounds −1 ≤ x, y, z ≤ 1 (or 0 ≤ z ≤ 1) describe where surviving points end up after the divide.

problem: 'Clipping is likely missing or applied after projection' is misleading: clipping is supposed to happen after projection, in clip space. The real failure is a missing near-plane / w > 0 test before the divide.
fix: Answer: the near-plane clip against w > 0 is missing, so a vertex behind the eye survives, gets a small or sign-flipped divided position, and drags its triangle into a spike across the screen.

problem: W is called 'its world matrix' but the formula p_world = W·M·p applies M as well, so W is really the parent chain's accumulated matrix and W·M is the object's world matrix. The two statements cannot both be right.
fix: Say: multiplying up the parent chain gives the parent's accumulated matrix W, so a local vertex becomes p_world = W·M·p, and the object's own world matrix is the product W·M.

problem: The fourth clip coordinate is written w_k in one sentence and w_c everywhere else, including the formulas just below.
fix: Use w_c throughout: 'the projection matrix copies z into the fourth clip coordinate w_c'.

problem: The text allows '(X, Y) is the viewport's lower-left or top-left origin', but the y formula y_px = Y + (1 − y_ndc)·H/2 only holds for a top-left origin with rows counted downward.
fix: Fix the origin: say (X, Y) is the top-left corner of the viewport in pixels and rows count downward; a bottom-left origin needs y_px = Y + (y_ndc + 1)·H/2.
